questions.question:
Choose the option that is the passive form of the sentence.

The doctor gave her an injection yesterday.

options.text: The doctor had given an injection for her yesterday
She is given an injection by the doctor yesterday.
She was gave an injection by the doctor yesterday.
She was given an injection by the doctor yesterday.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4, i.e.** '__She was given an injection by the doctor yesterday.'__

The given sentence is written in the **Simple Past Tense**.

The construction of the sentence:

**Subject + Verb + Object**

The doctor gave her an injection yesterday. 

The **Object** of the **Active voice** will become the '**Subject' of the passive voice** and the '**Subject'** of the **'Active voice'** will become the **agent **of the **passive voice.**

**​​**The construction of the **Passive voice**:

**Subject + Was/Were + past participle form of verb + by + agent**

 She was given an injection by the doctor yesterday.

Hence, **option 4** is the answer.

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence, which contains the grammatical error.

Those whose have lost their identity cards can get new ones issued from the office.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2, i.e.** '__Those whose have'.__

The segment '**Those whose have'** is erroneous. '**Whose'** is used to express '**of whom**' - to indicate something that belongs to or is associated with the person or thing mentioned in the previous clause. So, it cannot be used here. Instead, '**who**' will be a better fit which is used to specify the people.

Hence, **option 2** is the answer.

questions.question:
Choose the option that is the direct form of the sentence.

Anurag requested his employer for permission to leave office a little early that day.

options.text: Anurag asked his employer, "Please I can leave office a little early today?"
Anurag asked his employer, "Please, I will leave office a little early today?"
Anurag asked his employer, "Please may I leave office a little early today?"
Anurag asked his employer, "Please may I left office a little early that day?"

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anurag asked his employer, "Please may I leave office a little early today?"**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let's look at the steps to change the sentence from indirect to direct speech:
 
• When the direct speech is in an imperative form, we follow the steps given below:
 
 
• Change the sentence in the direct speech from imperative to assertive.
 
• The tense of reported speech is changed only when the reporting verb is in the past tense. 
 
• The reporting verb said to will replace **requested.**
 
• 'To infinitive' is replaced by a comma and inverted commas followed by the word 'please'.
 
• 'to leave' changes into 'leave'.
 
• Similarly 'to leave' changes into 'leave'.
 
 
 
• At last line up the remaining part.

 

Following these steps, we finally get- *Anurag asked his employer, "Please may I leave office a little early today?"*

questions.question:
Choose the option that is the indirect form of the sentence.

"Have you heard this story?" Neelu asked me.

options.text: Neelu asked me if had I heard this story
Neelu asked me if I had heard that story
Neelu asked me that if I had heard this story
Neelu asked me if I had hear that story

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neelu asked me if I had heard that story**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in Direct Speech. As per the question we have to change it into Indirect Speech. 
 
• The process of transformation as follows: 
 
 
• The given question is an example of an Interrogative sentence. 
 
• 'Said to' will be changed into 'asked'. 
 
• 'If' conjunction will be added to represent whether something is true or not
 
• An interrogative statement is converted into an assertive statement. Thus, the helping verb will be placed after the subject.
 
• **'You'** will be changed into 'I'. (according to the object of the reporting verb 'me')
 
• **'this**' will be changed into 'that'.
 
• **'Have'** will be changed into 'had' (Present perfect tense->Past Perfect tense)

 
 
 

Therefore the correct answer is: *Neelu asked me if I had heard that story*.

questions.question: The greatest disadvantage of the informal sector is that ______.

options.text: it pays lower and unequal salaries.
workers do not get security of work
it has fewer opportunities for movement
labour legislation does not reach workers

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4, i.e.** '__labour legislation does not reach workers.'__

According to the passage, " *However, the informal sector does not guarantee economic security, legal protection, equal and fair wages and workers' rights. The workers in this sector therefore land in a very vulnerable situations as the labour legislation or trade union organisation cannot reach there."* Clearly. the greatest disadvantage of the informal sector is that labour legislation does not reach workers.

Hence, **option 4** is the answer.

questions.question: Which sectors have the largest share of informal employment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3, i.e.** __'construction and trade'.__

According to the passage, "*Construction and trade are the two sectors that share a dominant part of informal employment with 76 percent and 72 percent respectively of all the workers in the non-agriculture, informal sector.*"

**Construction and trade** are the two sectors that have **the largest share of informal employment.**

Hence, **option 3 **is the answer.

questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT a reason why more women are found in the informal sector?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4), i.e.** '__higher wage'__.

According to the passage, "*Further, women are employed more in the informal sector because they are considered to be a cheap source of labour."*

'**Higher wage**' is definitely not the reason why more women are found in the **informal sector.**

Hence,** option 4 **is the answer.

questions.question: What is the percentage of women workers in the informal sector?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4, i.e.** '__more than 90'.__

**According to the passage**, "*More than 90 percent of women workers are employed in the informal sector".* Clearly '**more than 90'** should be chosen here.

Hence, **option 4** is the answer.

questions.question: Which statement is NOT true according to the passage?

options.text: The workers in the informal sector face several types of inequalities
In India, the contribution of the informal sector to the economy is large
Only women workers are employed as domestic workers and waste pickers
In India, informal trades from one-fourth of the urban employment sphere

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3), i.e.** '__Only women workers are employed as domestic workers and waste pickers.__'

 
• **Option 1, i.e.** '**The workers in the informal sector face several types of inequalities'** is true because it is mentioned in the passage that "*However, the informal sector does not guarantee economic security, legal protection, equal and fair wages and workers' rights."* 
 
• **Option 2, i.e. 'In India, the contribution of the informal sector to the economy is large'** is true because it is mentioned in the passage that "*Over 90 percent of workers in India are in the informal segment, which gives a significant share to the economy."*
 
• **Option 3, i.e. 'Only women workers are employed as domestic workers and waste pickers'** is a false statement because in the given passage it is mentioned that '*Nearly 25 percent of India's urban employment is dominated by four informal trades: domestic workers, home-based workers, street vendors, and waste pickers.' *In the passage it is not mentioned that only women workers are employed as domestic workers and waste pickers.
 
• **Option 4 i.e. 'In India, informal trades from one-fourth of the urban employment sphere.'** is a true statement. According to the passage, "*Nearly 25 percent of India's urban employment is dominated by four informal trades."*

 

Hence, **option 3** is the statement that is **not true.**

questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Pick the option that gives their correct order.**

A. It was there that he and his colleagues performed several experiments on light.

B. His curiosity was aroused and he got off the tram.

C. One day, when riding to work on a tram, Raman spotted a signboard with the words "Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science."

D. He walked into the building that was to become his laboratory.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2, i.e.** '__CBDA'.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• The first sentence is **C**, "*One day, when riding to work on a tram, Raman spotted a signboard with the words "Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science."*, because it has started to tell a story.
 
• The next sentence is **B**, "*His curiosity was aroused and he got off the tram."* because it says what Raman did after finding the signboard.
 
• The third sentence is **D**, "*He walked into the building that was to become his laboratory.*" because what he did after getting off the tram is mentioned here.
 
• The fourth sentence is** A**, "*It was there that he and his colleagues performed several experiments on light.*" because it is answering the question "how did he use the laboratory?".

 

Hence, **option 2** is the answer.

questions.question:

questions.question:
Select the alternative that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case there is no improvement select "No improvement"

He __walked very slow__ down a narrow path from his hut to the well.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4, i.e.** '__walked very slowly__.'

The word '**slow'** is an '**Adjective'** and an '**Adjective**' is not used to qualify a 'verb'. In order to qualify the verb '**walked**', an adverb should be used. So, '**Slowly'** should be used instead of the adjective '**slow**'.

Hence, **option 4** is the answer.
